title: Config validation rejects an adapter whose type isn't registered
description: coreconfig.Load()'s Validate() checks every configured adapter.Config.Type against adapter.IsRegistered() before the connector starts — a typo'd or unsupported type must fail fast at startup, not surface as a confusing runtime error later.
preconditions: A config.yaml with one adapter entry whose type is not one of rest|ldap|sql|ssh|winrm
steps: Call coreconfig.Load with the malformed config
Inspect the returned error
expectedResult: Load returns a *ValidationError naming the unregistered type; the connector does not start.

title: Config validation reports every schema violation in one pass, not just the first
description: ValidationError.Errors collects all violations (missing tenant_id, unregistered adapter type, missing adapter name, ...) in a single Load() call so a misconfigured connector reports everything wrong at once rather than one round-trip per fix.
preconditions: A config.yaml with 3 independent, unrelated validation problems
steps: Call coreconfig.Load
Inspect ValidationError.Errors
expectedResult: All 3 problems are present in Errors, not just the first one encountered.

title: connectorIdentityFromCert requires a non-empty CommonName and OrganizationalUnit
description: The connector recovers connector_id (CN) and tenant_id (OU) from its own issued certificate rather than persisting a second, driftable copy. Both a missing CN and a missing/empty-string OU must be rejected explicitly.
preconditions: A real, parseable self-signed certificate built via x509.CreateCertificate
steps: Call connectorIdentityFromCert with CommonName set and OrganizationalUnit omitted
Call connectorIdentityFromCert with CommonName set and OrganizationalUnit set to a single empty string
expectedResult: Both calls return a non-nil error naming the missing/empty OrganizationalUnit; neither silently accepts an empty tenant_id.
linkedDefect: VTEC-internal (found during Phase 8 live wiring, no external tracker ID)

title: Ed25519 envelope signature round-trips: sign then verify succeeds; a tampered payload fails
preconditions: A generated Ed25519 keypair via envelope.LoadOrCreateSigningKey
steps: Build an envelope and sign it with the private key
Verify the signature with the matching public key
Flip one byte of the signed payload and re-verify
expectedResult: The first verification succeeds; the second (tampered) verification fails.

title: SQL adapter checks the query allow-list before ever opening a database connection
description: RunQuery consults the shared AllowList before touching a.db — enforcement order is proven against both a real fixture and a deliberately unreachable port, so the check can't be bypassed by a target that never responds.
preconditions: An adapter configured with allow_list not containing the query name under test
steps: Call RunQuery with a query name absent from allow_list, target pointed at an unreachable port
Observe whether any connection attempt was made
expectedResult: The call is rejected with an allow-list error before any dial attempt — no connection-refused error, only the allow-list rejection.

title: Mask stage fails safe: a field absent from the allow-list is stripped, never passed through
description: mask.New(allowList) is deny-by-default — an unlisted field must never leak, since Mask is the last on-premises control before Encrypt/Queue/Upload.
preconditions: A Record with fields {"username": "x", "ssn": "123-45-6789"} and an allow-list of ["username"] only
steps: Run the record through Mask.Process
expectedResult: The output Fields contains only "username" — "ssn" is absent, not empty-stringed or nulled (fully removed).

title: Dedupe computes ContentHash over normalized+filtered Fields and drops an exact repeat
description: A second Collect() cycle producing byte-identical (post Normalize+Filter) content is intentionally dropped — Pipeline.Run returns (nil, nil) rather than an error, per the documented 'intentional drop, not a failure' contract.
preconditions: Two Records with identical Fields, run through the same Dedupe instance back to back
steps: Run record A through Dedupe.Process
Run record B (identical content) through Dedupe.Process
expectedResult: Record A passes through; record B returns (nil, nil) — an intentional drop, not an error.

title: Compress stage reports a genuine CompressionRatio, not a hardcoded constant
preconditions: A Record with highly repetitive test content (compresses well) and one with high-entropy random content (compresses poorly)
steps: Run both records through Compress.Process
Compare the two resulting CompressionRatio values
expectedResult: The repetitive content's ratio is meaningfully lower than the random content's — the value is computed as len(compressed)/len(plaintext), not a fixed number.

title: Client.Connected() reflects the real live connection state, not just 'was constructed'
steps: Call Connected() before Start()
Call Start() against a real test server and wait for the connection to establish
Call Connected() again
Close the underlying connection and call Connected() a third time
expectedResult: Connected() returns false, then true, then false — tracking the actual TLS connection object, not client lifecycle alone.

title: relayKeyProvider base64-decodes the relay-resolved credential into raw AES-256 key bytes
description: The Vault-stored value is base64 of a raw 32-byte key; relayKeyProvider.Key() must decode it correctly and return exactly 32 bytes, or Encrypt.Process would silently use the wrong key length.
preconditions: A fake relay.Client resolving a known base64-encoded 32-byte value for the encryption key ref
steps: Call relayKeyProvider.Key(ctx)
Inspect the returned byte slice's length and content
expectedResult: Returns exactly the 32 decoded bytes; a malformed (non-base64) resolved value returns an error, not a truncated/garbage key.
